question: What is the age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?
explanation: The World Health Organization specifically defines the adolescent bracket as spanning from age 10 through 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why might two teenagers of the exact same age look and grow quite differently?

options.A: Chronological age has no relation to physical growth
options.B: Physical changes stop completely after the tenth birthday
options.C: Biological maturation timings vary due to genetics and nutrition
options.D: Hospitals calculate age using different international standards

explanation: Every body has its own unique timetable! While age is just a number, how we grow depends a lot on our genes and nutrition. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h1)

question: During which phase of adolescence do teenagers really start thinking deeply and caring a lot about what their friends think?
explanation: Middle adolescence is when deep peer loyalty kicks in and teenagers start exploring more abstract, big-picture thinking. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between an 'adolescent' and 'adolescence'?

options.A: One is the person, and the other is the transitional process
options.B: One applies only to males, and the other only to females
options.C: They are completely identical terms used interchangeably
options.D: One refers to physical growth, and the other to mental illness

explanation: Think of it this way: the adolescent is the human being, and adolescence is the exciting stage of life they are walking through! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does the United Nations generally define the age bracket for youth?
explanation: The United Nations uses 15 to 24 years as its statistical definition for the global youth population. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is the term 'youth' viewed more as a social stage rather than just a fixed age group?

options.A: It only applies to individuals living in urban environments
options.B: It focuses heavily on social roles, independence, and economic status
options.C: It is determined entirely by the onset of puberty hormones
options.D: It is a fixed medical diagnosis made by physicians

explanation: 'Youth' is all about moving into the adult world—finding work, gaining independence, and taking on new social responsibilities. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of these terms specifically refers to the human being experiencing this phase of growth?
explanation: The adolescent is the actual person, while terms like adolescence and youth describe the time periods or social stages. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h4)

question: A community nurse is writing a report about job hunting and financial independence among 22-year-olds. Which term is best to use?
explanation: Since the focus is on jobs and independence for a 22-year-old, 'youth' is the most accurate and professional term to use. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h4)

question: As teenagers grow up, what is the biggest change that happens in their social lives?

options.A: Social interaction with others stops completely
options.B: Peer groups become the primary frame of reference
options.C: Family units become the sole source of social interaction
options.D: Work colleagues replace all school friendships

explanation: It's totally normal for teens to lean more on their friends and peer groups as they figure out who they are! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why do teenagers sometimes take big risks or act on impulse?

options.A: Brain development is completely finished by age ten
options.B: Parents encourage dangerous activities to build character
options.C: Teens explore identity and independence while their decision-making brain regions mature
options.D: Risky behaviors are mandatory symptoms of hormonal disease

explanation: The brain's impulse-control center is still under construction during these years, which explains why teens love quick thrills and trying new things. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h5)

question: What does the acronym HEADSS stand for in adolescent nursing assessments?

options.A: Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide
options.B: Heart, Ears, Abdomen, Drugs, Skin, Skeleton
options.C: Health, Exercise, Anatomy, Diet, Sleep, Symptoms
options.D: Hospital, Environment, Age, Diagnosis, Surgery, Status

explanation: HEADSS is a psychosocial screening tool used to evaluate key areas of an adolescent's life. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is keeping things confidential so vital when caring for teenagers?

options.A: It stops teenagers from needing any physical examinations at all
options.B: It guarantees that the adolescent will never experience an infection
options.C: It encourages teenagers to truthfully disclose sensitive health and lifestyle information
options.D: It is a legal requirement that prevents parents from ever knowing their child is sick

explanation: Teens worry about being judged. When we promise confidentiality, we build the trust they need to open up and tell us the truth about their health. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h6)
